intro: Bans online money games — any online game played by paying money in the hope of winning more, whether it's based on skill or chance (including fantasy sports, rummy and poker for stakes). It promotes e-sports and online social games. In force since 1 May 2026.

sections.p: No one can offer, operate or help offer online money games, whether the game is skill-based or chance-based. Banks and payment providers can't process transactions for them.
Advertising or promoting online money games in any media, including by celebrities and influencers.
sections.pen: Up to 2 years and/or ₹50 lakh; stricter for repeat offences

sections.p: The penalties target operators, promoters and facilitators — people who play are treated as victims rather than offenders.
E-sports are recognised as a legitimate competitive sport and can have entry fees and performance-based prizes, but no betting. Online social and educational games without money stakes are promoted.
A central Online Gaming Authority of India decides which games are money games, registers e-sports and social games, and handles complaints. Designated cyber police can investigate offences.
Tamil Nadu had already banned online gambling through its 2022 law; the central Act now applies across India.
